issues.legal_issue: For land-ceiling purposes, a family is a statutory unit based on the specified relationships, and a prior partition does not prevent minor sons’ separately held land from being counted in the family holding.
material_facts: A parent had partitioned property with his two minor sons before the appointed day, and each son held land separately under that partition.
The sons were minor members of the parent’s family on the appointed day.
The land-ceiling authority included the sons’ separately held land when determining the family’s holding.
issues.conclusion: The minor sons’ separate land had to be included in the family holding despite the prior partition.
issues.legal_principle: Section 2(10) defines a family by relationships, not by joint title or joint holding. Sections 4(1) and 4(2) make the family the unit for determining the ceiling and deem land held individually or jointly by family members to be held by the family. Section 4(3)(a), which separately addresses an individual’s share in an undivided Hindu family, confirms that the statutory family is distinct from a Hindu joint family. Section 4(4) addresses transfers and partitions made after the appointed day and before the Act commenced; it does not make the existence of a prior partition relevant to whether minor sons fall within the statutory family. No earlier cases are relied on.

predicates.land_ceiling_proceeding: An authority or court is determining the land holding of a family for a ceiling limit.
predicates.parent_child_family_relationship_exists: A person has minor children who are members of that person’s family for the ceiling determination.
predicates.minor_children_hold_land_separately_afte: The minor children hold land separately following a partition from their parent.

issues.definition: When a land-ceiling proceeding concerns a family relationship and minor children hold land separately after partition, their separate land is counted in the family holding.

issues.legal_issue: Land separately owned by a spouse is included when calculating the holding of the statutory family for land-ceiling purposes, even if the spouse acquired it with separate personal funds.
material_facts: The parent’s wife separately owned land that she had purchased using her Sridhanam money.
The parent and his wife were members of the same family for the ceiling determination.
The land-ceiling authority included the wife’s land in calculating the family holding.
issues.conclusion: The wife’s separately owned land had to be included in the family holding.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 2(10) and 4(2) define the family by relationship and deem land held individually by family members to be held by the family for ceiling purposes. Explanation IV to section 7(1) proceeds on the basis that separately held land of both spouses is pooled for the ceiling calculation; it allocates any land to be surrendered between them in proportion to their separate holdings. The source of the wife’s funds does not remove her land from the family calculation. No earlier cases are relied on.

predicates.land_ceiling_proceeding: An authority or court is determining the land holding of a family for a ceiling limit.
predicates.spouses_are_members_of_same_family: The landholder and spouse belong to the same family for the ceiling determination.
predicates.spouses_hold_land_separately: The spouses each hold land in their own separate ownership.

issues.definition: When a land-ceiling proceeding concerns spouses in the same family who hold land separately, the separately owned spousal land is counted in the family holding.
